title: Rick & Morty Explain: Monoliths vs Microservices!
caption: Why your app might be a 'Pickle Rick' or a 'Mr. Poopybutthole'! #SoftwareArchitecture

scenes.script: Alright, Morty, let's talk about software architecture. Imagine you're building a sandwich. A monolithic app is like one giant sandwich, with all the ingredients stuck together.
scenes.web_image: sandwich with all ingredients mixed together

scenes.script: Wait, so if I want to change the cheese, I have to rebuild the whole sandwich? That sounds like a bad time.
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png
scenes.web_image: person struggling to rebuild a sandwich

scenes.script: Exactly! Monolithic apps are simple at first, but changing one part can be a nightmare. It's like trying to modify a car while it's driving down the road.
scenes.web_image: mechanic working on a moving car

scenes.script: So what's the alternative? A bunch of tiny sandwiches that communicate through portals?
Close enough, Morty. Microservices break the app into small, independent services. Each does one thing, like a cheese service, a meat service, and so on.
scenes.web_image: separate containers for different sandwich ingredients

scenes.script: So if I want to change the cheese, I just build a new cheese service and plug it in? That sounds like a much better time.
You got it, Morty. Each service can be developed, deployed, and scaled independently. It's like having a team of tiny chefs, each making one part of the sandwich.
scenes.web_image: small chefs preparing different parts of a dish

scenes.script: But wait, how do these services talk to each other? Do they use the portal gun?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty evil with a serious looking and a portal gun.png

scenes.script: No, Morty. They communicate via APIs—like little messengers that go back and forth. It's like having a waitstaff in a restaurant, taking orders to the kitchen.
So microservices are better? Why would anyone use monolithic then?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png

scenes.script: Monolithic is simpler for small projects. Imagine you're just making a sandwich for yourself, not a restaurant full of customers.
Okay, so which one is better for a big project? Like... the Citadel?
Microservices! They scale better, you can update services independently. Just like the Citadel—one part breaks down, but the rest keeps running!
So if I want to build something big and not go crazy, microservices are the way to go. Got it!
Exactly! And remember, Morty—if your app is a mess, just say 'Wubba Lubba Dub Dub' and transition to microservices!
scenes.web_image: person shouting Wubba Lubba Dub Dub

topic: What is the difference between monolithic and microservices architecture?
